g.title: GaussLegendreFullExecution
g.text: Horizontal: six phases from physical inputs to validated Solution. Vertical: operations and numerical details.
Blue: common contracts. Orange: method preparation. Green: numerical algorithm. Purple: optional observation.
m = physical state size; q = internal workspace size; T = requested samples. All module paths are repository-relative.

g.title: RunMethod
g.text: SAME NUMERICAL CLASS / ONE INSTANCE PER EXECUTION
No separate context or callback-based method record.
Construct another instance for another integration.
Completed runs cannot re-enter the global driver.

save requested samples; report temporal progress.

g.text: Store dynamics, formulation and solver controls on self.

g.text: Analytic independent planar blocks when supported;

g.title: Stages
g.text: Extract physical samples and optional k history.
Stage quadrature advances k; output uses H+k.
Only accepted states continue the main trajectory.
Output sampling does not replace accepted nodes.

g.title: Legend
g.text: Thick arrows between phase headers: overall lifecycle; phases 04 and 05 repeat together for each main step.
Thin solid arrows: calls or required data. Dotted blue arrows: returned values. Dashed purple arrows: optional events.
A hollow diamond means a record contains another record. Red dashed arrows indicate failure propagation.
Card subtitles distinguish actual APIs from inline operations and numerical contracts.
The method prepares and advances; the controller selects accepted intervals and samples them.
The common coordinator records, observes and exports; the per-run collector owns history.
Method-specific Detail never becomes an implicit event history. Optional observers own analysis and persistence.
Fixed methods retain their fixed-step algorithms. DOP853 and Radau retain their adaptive numerical sessions.

g.title: Recording
g.text: ONE RUN / REQUESTED SAMPLES + ACCEPTED METRICS
Copy metric rows with stable keys and shapes.
Never store method details or observer events.
Rejected adaptive trials have no accepted row;
their numerical work belongs to the accepted step.

g.title: EventBuilder
g.text: Only called when an observer is installed.
Use accepted details and independent snapshots.

g.title: PhaseOutput
g.text: Finalize, validate and interpret the trajectory

g.title: Data
g.text: extracts the physical state and optional energy.
Export never repeats the numerical projection.
Internal and physical dimensions may differ.
Return to the original SimulationRunner call.
Only the requested trajectory is exposed by default.

g.title: Events
g.text: Two converged stage snapshots and fixed map_state.
The physical tangent can use the ideal-root equation.
An observer may analyze or retain records.
Default integration does not store event histories.

g.title: Failure
g.text: Stop the run; do not construct a successful
Retain method, time and solve context.

g.title: Snapshots
g.text: Two converged stage snapshots and fixed map_state.
The physical tangent can use the ideal-root equation.
Changing an event must not change integration
state, samples, subsequent events or metrics.

g.title: DiagnosticFields
g.text: residual norms and tolerance, plus legacy aliases.
One accepted nonlinear solve per step.

g.title: Resume
g.text: Require exactly the requested output times.
Check shape, finiteness and packed layout.
Verify that the initial state is preserved.

g.title: Solution
g.text: Owns copies of trajectory and diagnostic arrays.

g.title: Interpret
g.text: Solution carries physical samples and diagnostics.
Studies compose runs and reference comparisons.
do not by themselves establish trajectory accuracy.
